prompt.context: Our client is PLD, a global manufacturer of snack foods and beverages. PLD has been a market leader in China's potato chips (PC) market for over two decades. This year, the company's volume share in the South China region declined sharply from 60% to 20%. The company has hired us to find out why this happened and how to react.
prompt.question: How would you approach diagnosing the root cause of PLD's market share loss in South China, and what would you recommend the client do?

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the national PC market and PLD's national share?
clarifying_info.a: Last year PLD recorded 500,000 tons of sales in the national PC market with 40% share, followed by WWT (10%) and DLT (5%). Total national market was about 2,000,000 tons (implied by share data; note: South China is 10% of national volume).

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the South China market and who are the competitors there?
clarifying_info.a: South China accounts for 10% of the overall national PC market. Last year PLD sold 120,000 tons in South China with 60% share. WWT held 20% (40,000 tons) and DLT held 20% (40,000 tons). Total South China market was 200,000 tons.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the consumer segments in the potato chips market?
clarifying_info.a: There are two groups: Fun Seekers (prefer current fried products for crispy mouth feel) and the LOHAS group (strongly demand baked products with less or no oil). Fun Seekers make 80% of total market consumption but more people are switching to the LOHAS group.

clarifying_info.q: Are current potato chips products differentiated by price?
clarifying_info.a: Consumers see current potato chips as commodities, so average price is similar across competition. All current products are fried; PLD is considering introducing baked products using minimal or no oil.

exhibits.title: South China and National Volume by Player (Prior Year)
exhibits.shows: A table comparing each competitor's volume share and absolute volume (tons) in South China versus the national PC market for the prior year.

exhibits.title: Current Year South China Volume Data (Through September)
exhibits.shows: Prompts and data points to support the step-by-step diagnosis of the volume share change in South China, covering PLD's YTD volume, competitor volume growth, and the new entrant XCD's sales.

framework: 1. Diagnose the share change: decompose Volume Share = Volume / Market Size to determine whether share loss was driven by PLD volume decline or market size change
2. Investigate competitor dynamics: assess whether existing players (WWT, DLT) drove growth or whether a new entrant disrupted the market
3. Understand the new competitor: identify who entered, what they sell (product innovation), and who is buying (consumer segment shift)
4. Assess the strategic threat: evaluate whether the threat is short-term/regional or long-term/national
5. Recommend a response: short-term tactics to protect existing business and long-term strategy to compete in the baked products segment

questions.prompt: PLD's volume this year in South China is 100,000 tons through end of September. What does this tell you about PLD's performance?
questions.guidance: The candidate should compare YTD volume to the prior-year equivalent (9 months) and note that PLD's volume actually grew ~10%, not declined. This means the share drop from 60% to 20% was NOT caused by PLD losing customers — it was caused by the total market growing dramatically. The candidate should then calculate the implied current market size.

math.setup: Prior year South China full-year volume = 200,000 tons. Assuming no seasonality, prior year 9-month volume = 200,000 * 9/12 = 150,000 tons. PLD's prior year 9-month volume = 120,000 * 9/12 = 90,000 tons. PLD's current YTD volume = 100,000 tons. Implied current market size = PLD volume / PLD share = 100,000 / 20% = 500,000 tons.
steps: Prior year South China 9-month volume: 200,000 * 9/12 = 150,000 tons
Implied current market size: 100,000 / 0.20 = 500,000 tons YTD
Market size growth: from ~150,000 (prior year 9-month) to 500,000 tons — roughly 3.3x increase
math.answer: PLD's volume grew ~10%; the market itself grew dramatically (~3x), explaining the share collapse from 60% to 20%.

questions.prompt: WWT and DLT volumes are also growing at 10% this year. What does this imply about the source of market growth?
questions.guidance: If all three incumbents are growing at only 10%, the combined incumbent volume is ~220,000 tons YTD, well below the total 500,000-ton market. This means new entrants account for the majority of market growth. An excellent candidate quantifies the gap.

math.setup: Combined prior-year 9-month volume of PLD+WWT+DLT = 150,000 tons. At 10% growth, current combined = 150,000 * 1.10 = 165,000 tons (approximate). Alternatively: (120,000+40,000+40,000) * 9/12 * 1.10 = 200,000 * 9/12 * 1.10. Market total is 500,000 tons. New entrant volume = 500,000 - ~220,000 = ~280,000 tons.
steps: Incumbent combined last year full year: 200,000 tons
Incumbent combined YTD at 10% growth: 200,000 * (9/12) * 1.10 = 165,000 tons (approx)
New entrant volume: 500,000 - 220,000 ≈ 280,000 tons (majority of market)
math.answer: New entrants account for roughly 280,000 of 500,000 tons YTD — more than half the market. Incumbents are growing modestly; the disruption is entirely from a new player.

questions.prompt: There is one new competitor, XCD, which entered in the middle of this year (3 months ago). How would you assess XCD's scale and velocity?
questions.guidance: An excellent candidate calculates XCD's monthly run-rate and compares it to PLD's to show how dramatically outpacing XCD is. XCD's 3-month total = 280,000 tons; monthly = ~93,000. PLD's 9-month total = 100,000 tons; monthly = ~11,000. XCD's monthly volume is more than 8x PLD's.

math.setup: XCD total volume YTD = 280,000 tons over 3 months. PLD total volume YTD = 100,000 tons over 9 months.
math.answer: XCD is selling more than 8 times PLD's monthly volume despite being only 3 months in market — an exceptionally fast ramp.

questions.prompt: Why is XCD performing so well? What consumer segment is driving their growth?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore 4Ps (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) and identify that the key differentiator is product — XCD introduced a baked (non-fried) potato chip. The LOHAS consumer group (health-conscious, prefer no-oil products) is the buyer. The candidate should reason that LOHAS was only 20% of the prior market but is now more than half, and that most of the new LOHAS consumers were previous non-users of potato chips (not switchers from Fun Seekers), since Fun Seeker group volume is still growing.

brainstorming.prompt: How should PLD react to XCD's entry and the LOHAS trend? What strategic options exist in both the short term and the long term?

categories.name: Short-term: Protect existing Fun Seekers base
ideas: Increase marketing investment targeting Fun Seekers in South China
Run promotions and loyalty programs to reinforce preference
Introduce new flavors or limited editions to excite and retain the fried-product segment
Defend shelf space and distribution channels against XCD

categories.name: Long-term: Compete in baked products
ideas: Develop and launch PLD's own baked potato chip product to capture the LOHAS segment
Leverage existing manufacturing scale and brand trust to accelerate new product launch
Consider acquiring XCD to gain immediate baked-product capability and market share
License baked production technology or partner with a supplier

categories.name: Long-term: Preempt national expansion by XCD
ideas: Expand PLD's own baked product nationally before XCD can scale out of South China
Use PLD's national distribution network as a competitive advantage
Signal to XCD and investors that PLD will compete aggressively, potentially deterring further investment in XCD

categories.name: Supply chain / innovation
ideas: Invest in baking technology R&D to achieve cost parity or advantage vs. fried
Evaluate co-manufacturing or contract manufacturing for baked products to accelerate speed-to-market
Assess raw material sourcing differences between fried and baked production

recommendation: In the short term, PLD's core fried-product business and Fun Seeker customer base remain intact (10% volume growth). PLD should invest in promotions, new flavors, and marketing to defend this base in South China and proactively protect other regions before XCD expands.

In the long term, the LOHAS trend is real and accelerating; XCD's South China success is likely a test market before a national rollout. PLD must launch its own baked potato chip product — either by developing one internally or by acquiring XCD — to compete for the growing LOHAS segment and prevent a replay of the South China share loss at national scale.
risks: XCD may expand nationally faster than PLD can develop and launch a baked product
PLD's acquisition of XCD may be expensive given XCD's rapid growth trajectory
A PLD-branded baked product may cannibalize its own fried product line if not positioned carefully
The LOHAS trend may slow, making a large investment in baked products less valuable than projected
next_steps: Conduct a feasibility study on baked product development (timeline, capex, taste/quality benchmarks)
Assess XCD's valuation and acquisition appetite
Develop a short-term South China defense plan (promotions, distribution, pricing)
Monitor XCD's geographic expansion signals to determine urgency of national baked product launch
